subject: general
question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Yamuna river?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tons River** is one of the largest and most important **tributaries** of the Yamuna River.
 
• It originates from the **Bandarpunch Glacier** in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand.
 
• The Tons River merges with the Yamuna near **Kalsi** in the Dehradun district of Uttarakhand.
 
• The river is known for its **rugged terrain and steep gorges**, making it a significant river in the Himalayan region.
 
• The Tons River is also popular for **adventure sports** like rafting due to its high-speed water currents.
 
• This river contributes significantly to the **water flow** of the Yamuna, especially during the monsoon season.
 
• It flows through regions rich in **biodiversity** and passes through dense forests and valleys.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Son River**__

 __
 
• The Son River is a **major tributary of the Ganga**, not the Yamuna.
 
• It originates from **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows through states like **Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar**.
 
• The river is known for its sandy riverbed and **seasonal flow variations**.
 
 
 
• **Teesta River**__
 __
 
• The Teesta River is a **tributary of the Brahmaputra**, not the Yamuna.
 
• It originates from the **Tso Lhamo Lake** in North Sikkim.
 
• The river flows through **Sikkim and West Bengal**, and then enters Bangladesh.
 
• It is a vital source of **irrigation and hydroelectricity** in the region.
 
 
 
• **Gomti River**__
 
 
• The Gomti River is a **tributary of the Ganga**, not the Yamuna.
 
• It originates from **Gomat Taal** (also known as Fulhar Lake) near Madhotanda in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The river flows entirely within **Uttar Pradesh** and passes through cities like Lucknow.
 
• The Gomti is considered sacred in Hindu tradition and is linked to **religious practices**.
